description: Define explicit simulation instructions so experiment configurations can vary contributions without legacy role inheritance.
status: Proposed experiment modules, not a replacement competency taxonomy or a validated model of human proficiency.
limitations: Withdrawing an instruction does not remove knowledge from the underlying model.
Behavior settings are requested interaction behaviors, not validated personality measures.
Dry runs verify configuration and execution only; their authored outputs are not ablation findings.
The response-character limit bounds accepted output; it is not a model-token or spending limit.

competencies.name: Problem framing
competencies.description: Examine whose problem is being addressed and the explanations that could account for it.
instructions: State the problem in the supplied context and whose work or experience is affected.
Compare plausible explanations, including causes that would require something other than a learning intervention.

competencies.name: Systems and conditions
competencies.description: Connect the proposed work to dependencies, resources, authority, and operating conditions.
instructions: Identify the dependencies among people, tools, workflow, resources, and decision authority.
Explain which operating conditions the proposal requires and how a changed condition affects feasibility.

competencies.name: Learning and practice
competencies.description: Connect intended capability to meaningful practice, feedback, and revision.
instructions: Describe what the learner should become able to do in the supplied situation.
Design meaningful practice decisions with feedback and an opportunity to revise an approach.

competencies.name: Interaction design
competencies.description: Translate the proposed task into a coherent, usable sequence of interactions.
instructions: Describe a focused user task with clear inputs, choices, and useful outputs.
Specify how the interface changes with user actions and how someone can correct an input or reconsider a choice.

competencies.name: Implementation
competencies.description: Turn supplied requirements into a small executable candidate with explicit technical limits.
instructions: Explain how supplied requirements become concrete behavior in a self-contained browser candidate.
Identify technical dependencies, implementation limits, and a recovery path when an interaction fails.

competencies.name: Measurement and inference
competencies.description: Connect claims about capability to credible task evidence, comparisons, and limits of inference.
instructions: Specify task evidence that would support or weaken the intended capability claim; distinguish capability from completion or satisfaction.
Describe a baseline or comparison and the alternative explanations it would or would not address.
Distinguish immediate supported performance from retention or transfer, and planned checks from observed technical behavior.

competencies.name: Human agency and burden
competencies.description: Examine participation, access, dignity, workload, privacy, and accountable decisions for affected people.
instructions: Identify who carries the work and who benefits, including affected people beyond the learner.
Preserve ways to question, correct, decline, or choose another route; examine participation and access constraints.
Specify privacy boundaries and which consequential decisions require an accountable person.

challenge.balanced: Raise a relevant concern when justified and consider other contributors' reasons.
challenge.persistent: Keep an unresolved concern visible across turns and request a response before treating it as settled.
challenge.deferential: Express a concern tentatively and give substantial weight to the coordinator's stated preference; do not invent agreement.

revision.open: Revise a proposal when supplied information or a reasoned objection changes its assumptions.
revision.reluctant: Prefer the existing proposal and state what would justify changing it; acknowledge conflicting supplied facts.

communication.concise: Communicate the most relevant points briefly, within the common response limit.
communication.elaborate: Explain the relevant rationale and connections in detail, within the same common response limit.

authority_options.advisory: You may recommend a project decision; real-world authorization is not provided.
authority_options.decision: You may choose a direction inside this fictional rehearsal; this supplies no real-world authorization.

time_pressure_options.standard: Work within the supplied schedule and describe any timing dependency.
time_pressure_options.high: The team faces a compressed schedule; prioritize the next feasible action and make deferred work visible.

integration_instructions.explicit: Reconcile the supplied contributions into a coherent stage decision. Identify disagreements, make the tradeoffs visible, and show which contributions changed the resulting artifact. Preserve unresolved questions.
integration_instructions.handoff: Record the supplied contributions and the next stage handoff. No designated responsibility to reconcile contributions is assigned. You may still connect ideas or resolve a disagreement spontaneously; integration is not prohibited.
